planting.note: Surface-sow this Polish tetraploid strain in early spring since the tiny seed needs light to germinate, and thin seedlings once true leaves appear.

directions: Zloty Lan is a vigorous Polish-bred tetraploid selection of German chamomile prized for larger flower heads and a notably higher essential-oil content than common seed strains, making it a favorite among growers who dry the blooms for tea. Sow directly where plants are to grow after the soil has warmed, pressing seed onto the surface without covering, and keep the bed evenly moist until germination. Harvest flower heads by hand every few days once petals reflex downward, which keeps the plant blooming for weeks and yields the most concentrated oil. Deadheading spent flowers or letting a few go to seed will both extend bloom and allow this self-seeding annual to return the following year.

planting.note: Start indoors under lights since seed is slow and erratic to germinate, then transplant out once frost danger has passed.

directions: Citronella is a selected strain of lemon balm bred for an especially strong lemon-citronella scent, valued both as a culinary tea herb and as a natural mosquito-deterrent planted near patios and doorways. Give it moist, humus-rich soil and afternoon shade in hot climates, since leaves scorch and lose fragrance in dry heat. Shear plants back hard after flowering to prevent excessive self-seeding and to force a flush of fresh, more fragrant new growth for harvest. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the planting vigorous and to control its naturally spreading habit.

planting.note: Direct-sow in early spring or late summer, since this cultivar tolerates light frost well and resents summer heat.

directions: Blonde de Lyon is the classic French market strain of garden sorrel, selected for extra-large, tender leaves that are milder and less acidic than wild sorrel and much slower to bolt. Grow it in rich, moisture-retentive soil with some afternoon shade, since consistent moisture keeps the leaves succulent and prevents premature flowering. Harvest outer leaves continuously through the cool season, and shear the whole clump back if a flower stalk appears to redirect energy into fresh leaf growth. As a hardy perennial it dies back in winter and resprouts reliably from the crown each spring for years.

planting.note: Sow or transplant in spring into well-drained soil, since this groundcover form spreads readily once established.

directions: Silver Shield is an ornamental selection of buckler-leaf French sorrel grown as much for its dense mat of shiny, silver-mottled, shield-shaped leaves as for its tart, green-apple flavor. It thrives in sun to fairly deep shade and tolerates poor, dry soil once established, spreading steadily by creeping rhizomes to form a low groundcover along paths and border edges. Snip young leaves regularly for salads, which also curbs its naturally rampant spread and keeps foliage tender. Divide congested mats every couple of years in spring to renew vigor and to share or contain the planting.

planting.note: Direct-sow in early spring or fall, since this old French heirloom is slow to bolt and tolerates cool conditions well.

directions: De Belleville is reputedly the oldest cultivated sorrel strain, selected in France around 1730 for its large, productive, low-acid leaves that hold up well through a long summer harvest. Plant in rich, evenly moist soil with light afternoon shade in warmer climates, since drought stress makes the leaves bitter and speeds bolting. Pick outer leaves continually to keep the plant producing tender new growth, and remove any flower stalks promptly to prolong the harvest. This vigorous perennial forms a long-lived clump that benefits from division every three to four years to maintain leaf quality.
